battle.name: 宋平劉子勛之戰
battle.brief: 宋明帝泰始二年（466）十一月，廣陵太守、尋陽王劉子勛在揚州治所舉兵反宋，殺揚州刺史劉道濟。朝廷遣征西將軍侯安都率中軍北上，先斷邗溝糧道，再築壘逼近，以偏廂車、床子弩等重型弩機壓制城頭，輔以撞車與雲梯破城，劉子勛敗亡。本卡羅馬弩砲即宋軍攻城序列中負責遠程壓制的弩砲型武器。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 交戰的一方是南朝宋朝廷：宋明帝劉彧以湘東王入承大統，於建康即位後改元泰始，以中軍為禁旅核心，宿衛與輜重由領軍、護軍分領，另令揚州、徐州、益州等州刺史與太守徵發州兵、鎮兵、郡兵及縣邑丁役，兵糧則循揚子江與江南運河北運。朝廷的指揮中樞是尚書令、中書令與給事中，重大出兵以詔書與中旨下達，被徵州郡先遣行軍司馬或軍司率部前出，再由大軍接應。叛的一方以廣陵太守、尋陽王劉子勛為核心：他在揚州治所廣陵城集郡兵、宗室屬戶與依附的豪右，殺死或逼走了朝廷任命的揚州刺史劉道濟，遣使向鄰郡傳檄，檄文中把起兵說成替宗室除害（檄文全文已佚，措辭各家記載不一），一度有淮南與江南的游兵鄉勇響應，但始終沒有北方政權的援助，鄰州刺史也未被拖入陣營，所以叛軍的基幹仍是一城之地。兩軍相持的地理核心是廣陵城與其外的水陸通道：城控揚子江北岸的古邗溝，北接淮水，南通建康，朝廷圍城的第一件事就是掐斷這條糧道，叛軍則靠城中存糧與城郊搶收的糧食硬撐。
countriesEn: The fighting pitted the court of the Southern Song against a rebel holding of the Yangzhou capital region. Emperor Ming of Song, Liu Yu, had taken the throne at Jiankang as Prince of Xiandong and adopted the Taishi era; the imperial centre was the Central Army, with the Leader of the Armies and the Protector General commanding the palace guard and the service train, while the governors of Yangzhou, Xuzhou and Yizhou were ordered to raise state troops, garrison troops, commandery militia and county levies, with soldiers and grain moving north along the Yangtze and the inland canals. The direction of the war lay with the Secretariat and the Department of State Affairs, and major operations were launched by imperial rescript and palace orders; provinces first sent forward a marching controller or an army director with a detachment, which the main army then joined. The rebel side was centred on Liu Zixun, Prince of Xunyang and governor of Guangling: he mustered the commandery garrison, the households of the royal clan and the local great families at Guangling, the seat of Yangzhou, killed or drove off the court-appointed governor Liu Daoji, and sent proclamations to the neighbouring commanderies presenting the rising as a clan remedy for the state — the full text of the proclamations is lost and the wording differs from account to account. For a time armed bands and village militia from the Huai and from south of the river answered him, but no northern government came to his aid and no neighbouring governor was drawn in, so the fighting core of the rebels remained one city. The geographical hinge of the campaign was the city of Guangling and its water and land approaches: the city commanded the ancient Hangou canal along the north bank of the Yangtze, linked northward to the Huai and southward to Jiankang, and the court's first act was to cut that supply line, while the rebels tried to hold out on the grain stored inside the walls and on what they could seize from the fields around the city.
people: 亂方主角是劉子勛。他是劉宋宗室，一般認為為彭城王劉義符之子，父早卒；他本人封尋陽王、出任廣陵太守，坐鎮揚州治所並握有揚州兵權。起兵後他以廣陵城為根據，自稱揚州刺史，遣使四方，同時有地方豪右與不滿朝廷的將吏被捲入其中，但劉子勛身邊並沒有能獨當一面的宿將，他所能倚仗的只是城防與一批被裹挾的郡兵。朝廷方面實際主持平叛的是征西將軍侯安都：明帝把中軍精兵與各州勤王之師交給他，使其自建康沿運河北上，會合諸軍於廣陵城下，先以斷糧與聲勢迫降，再進兵攻城，終於攻破城垣、追捕劉子勛。劉子勛敗亡之後首級送到建康；關於他最後的結局，傳世史籍說法略異，有稱其走投鬱洲為部下所斬者，亦有稱被追兵擒殺者，可以確定的是他既未能南下建康，也未能再據一城。朝廷方面的另一個關鍵人物是已故揚州刺史劉道濟，他在起兵初期即遇害，性命折在亂軍手裡，使朝廷一時失守揚州門戶；前任宿將沈慶之、尚書令柳元景都已於上年（465）相繼被明帝處死或逼死，兩人的死既抽空了平叛最需要的宿將，也讓劉子勛的起兵有了可以使用的口實。直接加深朝廷猜忌的是明帝寵臣戴法興，他數次進言構陷沈慶之，促成舊將之死，成為朝廷內部失和的關鍵一環。
peopleEn: The rebel chief was Liu Zixun, a member of the Song imperial clan, generally held to be a son of Prince Pengcheng Liu Yifu, who died early; Liu Zixun himself was Prince of Xunyang and governor of Guangling, holding the seat of Yangzhou together with its troops. After raising his banner he proclaimed himself governor of Yangzhou, worked from the walls of Guangling and sent envoys to the four quarters, and drew in local great families and officers discontented with the court; but he had no seasoned commander of his own and could rely only on the fortifications and on a commandery garrison pressed into the revolt. On the court side the suppression was actually led by Xulie Jiangjun Hou Andu: the emperor gave him the picked troops of the Central Army together with the relief forces of several provinces, and he moved north from Jiankang along the canal, joined the other armies beneath the walls of Guangling, first tried to starve the city into surrender and then assaulted it, breaking the ramparts and hunting down Liu Zixun. After his defeat his head was carried to Jiankang; the accounts of his final fate differ, some saying that he fled to Yuzhou and was killed by his own men, others that he was caught and killed by the pursuers, but it is certain that he neither reached Jiankang nor held another city. Another key figure was the late governor of Yangzhou Liu Daoji, who was killed at the very outset of the rising, so that the court lost the gateway of Yangzhou all at once. The former commanders Shen Qingzhi and Shangshu Ling Liu Yuanjing had both been put to death or driven to suicide by Emperor Ming in the previous year, 465; their deaths stripped the state of the very generals needed for the campaign while giving Liu Zixun a grievance to rally men around. The man who deepened the distrust was the emperor's favourite Dai Faxing, who repeatedly denounced Shen Qingzhi and brought about the death of the old general; his intrigues were a key link in the court's internal quarrels.
kits: 本卡的兵器是羅馬弩砲（scorpio）：以扭力簧片蓄力、一次發射一支重箭的架設式弩機，通常置於三腳木架或兩輪車架之上，箭鏃與箭桿合重接近一公斤，有效射程在數百米，居高臨下可壓制城牆與遠距散兵。中國戰場上並沒有這種西式扭力弩砲，與它最接近的是劉宋的偏廂車與床子弩：偏廂車把弩機裝在車側，用絞盤蓄力、逐發施放；床子弩則把大弩固定在低矮木架上，伏地或倚牆射擊。兩者與羅馬弩砲同屬「一發一矢、逐發補充」的重型弩機系統，只是蓄力改用人力絞索，射程與射速都受同一組限制。攻城序列中，弩砲級武器負責的是遠程火力壓制：對城頭守軍與觀望樓上的指揮官逐點射擊，掩護撞車、雲梯與攻城車靠近。真正破門的工具是木製撞車（撞木）、可移動的雲梯與飛雲梯，以及高數丈的攻城木城與樓車，遠程拋射仍靠投石車擲石，燒毀城頭的遮蔽物與女牆。守方的對應是弩、弓、礪石、滾木與門下的反衝，關鍵在於能否頂住連續的拋石與撞擊。作戰裝備方面，劉宋步卒以長槍與環首刀為主，騎兵比例不高，鎧甲多為熟革與札甲，弩手為求射速常不披重甲而靠塹壕與牆體遮蔽。軍需方面，弩矢按人限量配給並在營中補充，糧秣靠江淮水道運漕，攻守雙方都受制於水陸運輸線是否暢通。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman scorpio: a piece of artillery that stores its energy in torsion spring bundles and looses a single heavy bolt at a time, normally set on a wooden tripod or on a two-wheeled carriage. Bolt and shaft together weigh close to a kilogram, and the effective range runs to several hundred metres, which allows the engine to shoot down from a height onto a wall or to break up distant formations. No such Western torsion engine existed in China; the closest counterparts in the Liu Song were the pianxiangche, the bolt-thrower mounted on the side of a wagon and wound up by a capstan, and the chuangzi crossbow, a large crossbow fixed on a low frame for firing from the ground or against a wall. Both belong to the same family as the scorpio, a heavy machine that fires one bolt at a time and must be rewound after every shot, and both are limited in range and rate of fire by the same labour-intensive winding. In a siege order of battle the heavy crossbow class handled long-range suppression, picking off the defenders on the parapet and the commanders on the observation towers while the rams, scaling ladders and siege towers were brought forward. The instruments that actually opened the gate were the wooden battering ram, mobile scaling ladders and flying ladders, together with timber siege towers several fathoms high, while stones were thrown by catapults to smash the shelters and the parapet above the wall. The defenders answered with crossbows, bows, stones and logs rolled down the ramparts and with counter-shocks at the gate; everything turned on whether the wall could absorb the stone-throwing and the ramming. On the Chinese side the infantry fought mainly with long spears and ring-pommelled sabres, cavalry was a small proportion, and armour was mostly boiled leather and lamellar, the crossbowmen often going unarmoured to keep the rate of fire and trusting the ditch and the wall to cover them. In the service system crossbow bolts were issued by quota and replenished within the camp, while grain moved by barge along the waterways of the Yangtze and the Huai, so both sides remained at the mercy of whether the transport line stayed open.
tactics: 朝廷平叛的基本方針是先斷後打：主力自建康沿揚子江北上，入淮南之後分兵封鎖揚州境內的漕渠與渡口，斷掉廣陵城的水陸糧道，同時派使分化叛軍，宣布只誅首惡、脅從不問，用以孤立劉子勛。圍城之後，進攻方先在城外營壘築土山逼近城牆，把弩砲一類的重型弩機架在土山與營樓之上，壓制城頭守軍，掩護工匠連夜趕造雲梯與撞車；白日進逼、夜間施工是這類圍城的常態，用以避開守軍的投石與火攻。守方則利用廣陵既有的城垣與城壕反覆出擊，乘夜派敢死隊焚毀城下的撞車與雲梯、破壞進逼的土壘，並盡可能拖延糧盡的一刻。決戰出現在援軍與攻城器械同時就位之後：撞車集中撞擊城門與城牆薄弱之處，弩砲封住缺口，守軍在缺口被突破之後潰散，劉子勛出逃，戰事遂告結束。這一役並非大規模野戰會戰，而是典型的圍城與反圍城：交鋒集中在城門、塹壕與攻城器械一帶，勝負取決於哪一方能先把糧道與器械這兩件事做到底。
tacticsEn: The court's method was to cut the enemy off before beating him. The main force moved north from Jiankang along the Yangtze, and once in the Huai region it detached columns to seal the canals and the fords of Yangzhou and sever the water and land supply of Guangling, while envoys worked to split the rebel ranks, promising that only the leaders would be punished and that those who had been coerced would be let go, in order to isolate Liu Zixun. Once the city was invested, the besiegers first raised earthen works outside their camp so as to close on the walls, set the heavy crossbows on the mounds and the camp towers so that they could hold down the parapet, and used that cover to let the engineers build scaling ladders and rams by night. Approaching by day and working by night was the normal rhythm of such a siege, for it avoided the stones and the fire of the defenders. The garrison used the existing walls and ditch of Guangling for counter-strikes, sending bands of resolute men out at night to burn the rams and the ladders below the walls and to cut down the advancing earthworks, and it tried above all to hold out until the grain ran out. The decision came when the relief troops and the siege engines were both in place: the rams struck the gates and the thin parts of the wall in concentrated blows, the heavy crossbows covered the breach, and the defenders broke up once it was forced, Liu Zixun fled and the fighting was over. This was not a set-piece battle in the open but a textbook siege and counter-siege, fought around the gates, the ditch and the siege engines, and decided by which side managed to settle the two questions of the supply line and the siege machinery first.
data: 可考的時序是：宋明帝泰始二年（466）十一月，劉子勛在廣陵舉兵；至泰始三年（467）初，廣陵城破，亂事平定，前後約兩三個月。人物方面，揚州刺史劉道濟死於亂軍，宿將沈慶之卒於465年，尚書令柳元景卒於465年九月，說明朝廷在開戰時已無第一流宿將可用。地理上，廣陵城即今江蘇揚州，控揚子江北岸的古邗溝，南距建康約二百三十公里，水路是其間最便捷的運兵與運糧線；城自吳王夫差以來屢加修築，一直是揚州治所，也是淮南軍需的總匯之地。武器對照方面，羅馬弩砲的箭重接近一公斤，射程數百米，一發一矢，發射後須重新絞索蓄力；中國的偏廂車、床子弩受同樣的射程與射速限制，與之最為相近。至於雙方兵員、攻城器械數目與死傷數字，現存的《宋書》與《資治通鑑》都沒有留下可核的記載，因此可以確定的只有時序、距離、人物卒年與器械性能；兵力與死傷的具體數目，史無可考，於此不作虛構。
dataEn: The sequence that can be checked is this: in the eleventh month of the Taishi second year (466) Liu Zixun raised his banner at Guangling; by the beginning of the Taishi third year (467) the city had fallen and the rising was over, a matter of some two or three months. As for men: the governor of Yangzhou Liu Daoji was killed by the rebels, the old general Shen Qingzhi died in 465 and Shangshu Ling Liu Yuanjing died in September 465, which shows that the court had no first-class commander left when the war began. Geographically, Guangling is the present-day Yangzhou in Jiangsu, commanding the ancient Hangou canal on the north bank of the Yangtze, about 230 kilometres north of Jiankang by the easiest water route; the city had been rebuilt again and again since the reign of King Fuchai of Wu, remained the seat of Yangzhou throughout, and served as the collecting point for the military stores of the Huai region. For the weapon comparison: the bolt of a Roman scorpio weighs close to a kilogram and flies several hundred metres, one shot at a time, and the engine has to be re-wound with rope after every discharge; the Chinese pianxiangche and chuangzi crossbow are subject to very similar limits of range and rate of fire and are the closest analogues. The troop strengths of both sides, the number of siege engines and the casualty figures are simply not recorded in any verifiable way in the Songshu or the Zizhi Tongjian, so only the chronology, the distance, the death dates of the named figures and the performance of the engines can be stated with confidence; no specific numbers of troops or dead are invented here.
cause: 起義的直接背景是宋明帝即位後對宗室與功臣的系統性清洗。劉彧以湘東王身份繼位，前廢帝劉子業被廢黜並誅殺，隨即清洗廢帝一朝的重臣：沈慶之因求揚州刺史而觸怒皇帝，被戴法興構陷，賜死建康；柳元景因圖謀廢前廢帝，事發被誅；揚州刺史劉道濟在廣陵城破之前先行遇害。這幾步把劉宋最能打的將領與最能維持政局的樞臣一一拔除，等於向宗室與地方勢力表明，朝廷對自己人比對北敵更嚴酷。劉子勛方面，廣陵是他的封國所在，又是揚州治所，握兵、握財、握漕運；朝廷削藩與更換官吏時，廣陵正是首當其衝之地，軍民對新任上官的苛政與攤派怨言，成為他得以召募部眾的社會基礎。加上劉子勛本人具有宗室血統與較高的名分，號召力遠勝尋常的地方叛將，使這場兵變很快從地方抗命升級為對中央的公開挑戰。
causeEn: The immediate background to the rising was the systematic purge of the imperial clan and the meritorious officials that Emperor Ming carried out after his accession. Liu Yu came to the throne as Prince of Xiandong, the deposed emperor Liu Zhiye was deposed and killed, and the ministers of the late reign were then removed one by one: Shen Qingzhi, who asked to be made governor of Yangzhou and thereby offended the emperor, was denounced by Dai Faxing and put to death at Jiankang; Liu Yuanjing was executed for his plot to depose the previous emperor; and Liu Daoji, governor of Yangzhou, was killed at Guangling before the city fell. Each step removed from the state its best fighting men and its most capable administrators, and told the clan and the local powers that the court dealt more harshly with its own people than with the northern enemy. On Liu Zixun's side, Guangling was his own fief, the seat of Yangzhou, and gave him the soldiers, the revenue and the grain traffic of the province; when the court reduced the fiefs and replaced the officials, Guangling was the first place to feel it, and the complaints of the local people and of the soldiers against the new administrators gave him the social base from which to recruit. With his royal blood and his standing, his call to arms carried far more weight than that of an ordinary local rebel, and the rising soon turned from local disobedience into an open challenge to the centre.
impact: 這場平叛的政治後果遠大於戰果本身。明帝自此對宗室防範愈嚴，廣陵、彭城一帶的封國被大幅削弱，宗王多被徵入京師或外鎮而失去部曲，朝中宿將如侯安都雖立功，也因捲入後來的宮廷陰謀於泰始六年被誅，功臣與皇權之間的信任鏈再度繃斷。劉宋由此走向一個更集權也更脆弱的結構：皇帝靠猜忌維持統治，宗室與門閥則在私下的姻連與屬戶中尋求補償，南朝政局的裂痕越來越難以彌合。經濟與軍事層面上，廣陵之戰牽動揚州漕運與淮南兵糧的重新調配，州郡徵發與民夫運輸的負擔短期內加劇，國力再遭折損。北方的北魏在其內部改革尚未展開之際已大致整合完成，南朝卻把有限的資源耗在內部傾軋上，這一失衡成為日後劉宋覆亡與隋代統一江南的遠因之一。就史料而言，此役的過程細節多賴《宋書》本紀與《資治通鑑》卷一百三十五互相參校，雙方將領姓名與兵力數目多有缺佚，是研究南朝宗室政治的重要而殘缺的斷面。
impactEn: The political consequences of the settlement far exceeded the military result. Emperor Ming from then on watched the imperial clan more closely than ever: the fiefs around Guangling and Pengcheng were cut down, princes were summoned to the capital or sent to remote posts where they lost their private retainers, and a commander such as Hou Andu, who had earned his place in this war, was executed in the sixth year of Taishi after being drawn into later palace intrigues, so the chain of trust between soldiers and the throne was broken again. The Southern Song moved towards a structure that was at once more autocratic and more fragile: the emperor maintained rule by suspicion, while the clan and the great families sought compensation through private marriage alliances and through their own networks of dependents, and the fissures in southern dynastic politics grew harder to close. On the economic and military side the fighting at Guangling forced the grain traffic of Yangzhou and the military stores of the Huai to be reorganised, the burden of levies and of transport labour on the commanderies grew heavier in the short term, and the state was worn down again. In the north, the Northern Wei had already completed the great part of its own unification before its internal reforms were carried out, while the southern court spent its limited resources on internal fratricide; that imbalance was one of the distant causes of the later fall of the Liu Song and of the eventual Sui unification of the south. For the historical record the episode survives mainly in the annals of the Songshu read against Volume 135 of the Zizhi Tongjian, and the names of many officers on both sides and all strength figures are missing, which makes it an important and fragmentary window on the politics of the southern imperial clan.
result: 結果是劉子勛的政權在廣陵城被連根拔除：城破之後他未能再據一城，出逃時被殺（或說為部下所斬），首級與亂情一併送達建康，朝廷在淮南各處搜捕餘黨，響應的郡縣官員或被誅、或被貶官流放，脅從的士卒與鄉里武裝多獲赦免。泰始三年初亂平之後，明帝下詔大赦，重新釐定州郡賞罰以安江南人心，並把揚州防務與廣陵的郡縣建置收回朝廷直接控制，斷絕再出宗室割據的條件。從軍事層面看，這是一次代價不算太高、收益也有限的勝利：叛軍只在廣陵一地作戰，朝廷以中央禁軍與數州勤王之師迅速壓倒，戰略上並無出奇之處；真正被消耗的是劉宋的元氣與朝廷的信用——宗室與重臣接連喪命、一次大內亂必須平定，都加深了南朝「同姓相殘、外藩坐大」的病態。此役之後，劉宋表面上仍維持對江南的統治，其內部的裂痕卻已無從修補。
resultEn: The outcome was that Liu Zixun's regime was torn out of Guangling root and branch. After the city fell he could not hold another place; he was killed as he fled, or by his own men as some accounts have it, and his head and the news of the business were carried to Jiankang. The court hunted the remaining partisans through the Huai, and the officials of the commanderies who had answered him were executed, or exiled and demoted, while the soldiers and the village bands who had merely been coerced were mostly pardoned. Once the rising was settled in the early months of the third year of Taishi, the emperor issued a general amnesty, re-ordered the rewards and penalties of the commanderies to reassure the people of the south, and brought the defence of Yangzhou and the administration of Guangling once more under direct central control, removing the conditions for a princely separatism to arise again. At the military level this was a victory of no great cost and no great gain: the rebels fought in one city only and the court overwhelmed them quickly with the central army and the relief troops of several provinces, and there was nothing ingenious in the tactics. What was truly spent was the vigour of the Liu Song and the credit of the court — the deaths of princes and senior ministers one after another, and a large internal rising that had to be put down, all deepened the southern sickness of the clan destroying itself while the outer lords grew strong. After this the Liu Song still held the south in appearance, but its internal cracks could no longer be repaired.
